purpose: Compare outcome quality and resource use with the Design Council skill available versus the same model without the skill.

reporting_hierarchy.primary_question: Does Design Council produce a practically meaningful outcome-quality benefit over the no-plugin session?
reporting_hierarchy.basis: The preregistered quality uplift threshold was 3 points; the observed 9.285714-point uplift had a 95% case-bootstrap interval of [6.071429, 12.738095].
reporting_hierarchy.resource_note: The 1.5x token ratio is retained as an optimization target, not an outcome-value veto.

incremental_value.resource_basis: The 1.835622x token ratio exceeded the configured 1.5x optimization target.

post_hoc_outcome_profile.note: Candidate responses, blind judgments, the preregistered quality threshold, and resource measurements are unchanged. The reporting hierarchy, blind dimension aggregation, and overlapping construct groups are post-hoc additions and must be preregistered for a confirmatory rerun.

interpretation: On this internal Codex corpus, making Design Council available established a practically meaningful blind-rated outcome-quality benefit and removed the earlier technical-spike regression. The largest post-hoc dimension gains were evidence calibration, methodological rigor, and breadth/non-obviousness; overlapping construct groups were positive for right-problem framing, structured divergence, evidence discipline, learning/iteration, and appropriate scope. The aggregate token premium remained above the selected optimization target, but resource use does not negate the measured outcome benefit. This supports a quality-positive private beta; it does not establish monetary cost-effectiveness or native Claude efficacy.
limitations: The product team authored the prompt corpus and rubrics.
The judge was a model, not an independent human panel.
Candidate wording could reveal Design Council terminology even though arm labels were blind.
Six of 24 pairs changed winner across counterbalanced judge presentations.
Three candidate responses exceeded the shared 900-word cap.
Bundled host-runtime capabilities remained a shared environmental boundary.
The marginal metric is not monetary ROI and does not assign business value to a quality point.

This run compares the plugin with raw prompting. The separate frozen strong Design Thinking prompt-only comparison at evals/evidence/ab-benchmark-strong-prompt-beta3.json was inconclusive and did not establish incremental single-turn value beyond competent prompt engineering.

This is a single-turn Codex study. Held-out external prompts, independent human judges, multi-turn outcome studies, and a native Claude comparison remain necessary before a broad public efficacy claim.
